trial_court: 2nd Additional District Judge, Sabarkantha in Regular Civil Appeal No.9 of 2005
facts_of_case: The parties were married under the Hindu Marriage Act. The respondent filed an appeal against a judgment and decree passed by the trial court. The trial court had allowed the petition for divorce and awarded permanent maintenance to the wife.

legal_principles.principle: The right to appeal under the Hindu Marriage Act is provided in Section 28, and the applicability of the Code of Civil Procedure is only for laying down procedure and no more.
legal_principles.held: This Court held that the right to appeal under the Hindu Marriage Act is provided in Section 28 and the applicability of the Code of Civil Procedure is only for laying down procedure and no more.
cited_cases: LALLUBHAI KESHAVRAM JOSHI V/S. NIRMALABEN LALLURAM JOSHI, (1972) GLR 626

legal_principles.principle: The scope of exercise of jurisdiction by the High Court in Second Appeal under Section 100 is limited to substantial questions of law framed at the time of admission of the appeal or additional substantial questions of law framed at a later date after rewarding reasons for the same.
legal_principles.held: This Court held that as per settled law, the scope of exercise of the jurisdiction by the High Court in Second Appeal under Section 100 is limited to substantial questions of law framed at the time of admission of the appeal or additional substantial questions of law framed at a later date after rewarding reasons for the same.

legal_principles.principle: A point of law which admits of no two opinions may be a proposition of law but cannot be a substantial question of law.
legal_principles.held: This Court held that a point of law which admits of no two opinions may be a proposition of law but cannot be a substantial question of law.

legal_principles.principle: A substantial question of law must be a debatable, not previously settled by law on the land or a binding precedent and answer to the same will have a material bearing as to the rights of the parties before the Court.
legal_principles.held: This Court held that a substantial question of law must be a debatable, not previously settled by law on the land or a binding precedent and answer to the same will have a material bearing as to the rights of the parties before the Court.
cited_cases: Varshaben vs Janakkumar, (2010) X SCC Y

outcome.final_order: The marriage stands dissolved subject to the condition that the respondent deposits an amount of Rs.2 Lacs towards permanent maintenance within six months from the date of judgment and decree.
